BSB primary translation context for peace and contentment

observedEvidence: A contemporary mother and child sit together in a populated office waiting room with service desks and other waiting adults behind them.
The mother turns toward the child with relaxed shoulders and attentive expression; the child looks up speaking, rather than either person showing distress.
Settled attentive presence coexists with visible public-office activity; the scene does not imply circumstances must disappear to experience peace.
One coherent scene, no visible Bible text, generated title, logo or watermark.
reviews.scriptureContext: John 14:25-31 has Jesus reassuring his disciples about his departure, the Advocate and his own peace while adversity remains. A calm attentive adult amid public-office activity illustrates peace in circumstance; it does not replace Christ with breathing as the source of divine peace. Philippians 4:6-7 similarly locates peace in prayer and Christ.
limitations: Noise, housing-office purpose and an actual breath cannot be independently heard or proved from these still pixels; populated municipal-style office and listening are visibly supported.
The child’s exact question and the people’s faith are not inferable from pixels.
Scene role only: no rights, generated-source provenance, browser crop, title-overlay or release acceptance is asserted.

observedEvidence: A contemporary woman sits naturally in a visibly worn green armchair in an ordinary apartment, holding a plain mug with both hands.
Closed eyes, slight relaxed smile and settled posture visibly communicate peaceful contentment; modest furniture, ordinary knitwear and no luxury display support ordinary sufficiency.
One coherent photographic scene, no visible Scripture, rendered title, logo or watermark.
This is a thematic contemporary illustration, not a depiction of Paul or a historical biblical event.
reviews.scriptureContext: Philippians 4:10-14 addresses Paul receiving support and having learned contentment in plenty and need through Christ. An ordinary contented person is a permissible illustration; the mug or armchair is not presented as the source of spiritual contentment, nor as a promise of material prosperity.
limitations: The still image alone cannot demonstrate learned contentment through deprivation; the application must retain the approved source reference/context.
Overall uniqueness against all other artworks belongs to a separate independent reviewer.
Scene role only: no rights, generated-source provenance, browser crop, title-overlay or release acceptance is asserted.
